title: CRISPR Editing of Immortalized Cell Lines with RNPs using Nucleofection
author: Synthego
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.spnedme
materials: Count the cells to determine the cell density.
Extract DNA from cells 48 hours after transfection.

steps.title: Subculture cells to appropriate confluence
steps.instruction: Two days before nucleofection, subculture cells and seed them so that they reach 70–80 % confluence on the day of transfection; aim for ~1.5 × 10⁵ cells per nucleofection reaction.

steps.title: Pre‑warm destination growth medium
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm 1 mL of normal growth medium in each well of a 12‑well plate; this plate will receive the cells after nucleofection.

steps.title: Assemble CRISPR RNP complexes
steps.instruction: In appropriate tubes, combine Cas9 protein and sgRNA at a 3:1–9:1 molar ratio (example ratio 9:1). For knock‑in of inserts <50 bp, add 1 µL of 60 µM ssDNA HDR template per reaction; each homology arm should be ≥50 bp. Prepare the RNP solution according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Incubate RNPs before use
steps.instruction: Incubate the assembled RNP mixture at room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Detach and wash cells
steps.instruction: If using adherent cells, add enough TrypLE Express to cover the monolayer, incubate ~5 minutes until cells detach, then neutralize with at least twice the volume of normal growth medium. For suspension cells, spin down cells before each aspiration, aspirate medium and wash 1–2 times with an appropriate volume of 1× PBS, avoiding vigorous shaking that could cause clumping.

steps.title: Aliquot target cell number
steps.instruction: Count and aliquot enough cells to obtain 1.5 × 10⁵ cells for each nucleofection reaction.

steps.title: Pellet cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the aliquoted cells at 90 × g for 8–10 minutes at room temperature; handle the loosely packed pellet gently when removing supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in Nucleofector solution
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 5 µL of Nucleofector™ Solution per reaction. Work quickly and keep the cells in this solution for no longer than 15 minutes; avoid bubble formation.

steps.title: Combine cells with RNPs
steps.instruction: Add the 5 µL cell suspension to 25 µL of the prepared RNP solution, yielding a 30 µL cell‑RNP mixture per reaction.

steps.title: Load mixture into Nucleocuvette strip
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire 30 µL cell‑RNP mixture into a well of a Nucleocuvette™ strip, click the lid into place, and gently tap the strip on the benchtop to ensure the sample fully covers the well bottom and that no bubbles remain.

steps.title: Set up Nucleofector program
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate Nucleofector™ program for the cell type. Verify that the full Nucleofector Supplement has been added to the solution and that the mixture is less than 3 months old.

steps.title: Run nucleofection and post‑run incubation
steps.instruction: Place the sealed Nucleocuvette strip into the retainer of the 4D‑X Core unit, confirming orientation (larger cutout = top, A1/A2; smaller = bottom, H1/H2). Press “Start” and run the program; a green “+” indicates successful transfection. After the run, remove the strip. If the cell line requires it, incubate the strip at room temperature for an additional 10 minutes.

steps.title: Recover cells with growth medium
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL of pre‑warmed growth medium to each well of the Nucleocuvette strip, gently pipette up and down 2–3 times to resuspend the cells.

steps.title: Transfer cells to culture plate
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire 100 µL (30 µL mixture + 70 µL medium) from each well to the corresponding pre‑warmed 12‑well plate prepared in step 2.

steps.title: Post‑nucleofection incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the cells for 2–3 days in a humidified 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Assess editing efficiency and store cells
steps.instruction: Analyze editing by PCR, Sanger sequencing, and ICE analysis (or NGS, FACS, functional assays as alternatives). Optionally split the culture: one portion for analysis, the other for continued growth or cryopreservation.
